methods.label: Transfer the central angles to P
methods.explanation:
Join the centers to the tangency points. The resulting right angles let us transfer the arc measures to angles at \(P\).

[Figure 1](figures/1955_AMC_12_Q29_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(O_1\) and \(O_2\) be the midpoints of \(SR\) and \(RT\), respectively, so they are the semicircle centers. The marked arcs \(AR\) and \(RB\) have measures \(a\) and \(b\). Arc measure equals the corresponding central-angle measure, giving
\[
\angle RO_1A=a,
\qquad
\angle RO_2B=b.
\]
Construct a ray \(PH\) perpendicular to \(ST\), pointing toward the side containing the semicircles. In the displayed configuration, this ray lies inside \(\angle APB\).

The tangent \(PA\) is perpendicular to \(O_1A\). Turning both rays \(O_1R\) and \(O_1A\) counterclockwise through \(90^\circ\) gives directions parallel to \(PH\) and \(PA\), respectively. Turning both rays by the same amount preserves their angle, so \(\angle APH=a\).

Similarly, \(PB\) is perpendicular to \(O_2B\). Turning \(O_2R\) and \(O_2B\) clockwise through \(90^\circ\) gives directions parallel to \(PH\) and \(PB\), respectively. Thus \(\angle HPB=b\). Adding the two adjacent angles yields
\[
\angle APB=\angle APH+\angle HPB=a+b.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
